summary: The mechanism is plausible and the parity profile supports it (Marlin at bs=1 is 41 us for both GEMMs against an ~11 us floor, ~30% of HBM), the change is shape-gated to bs<=8 with four untouched control shapes, and the only landed hypothesis is the base pipeline itself, so there is nothing to revert or retune; the run's own per-kernel profile separates compact_routes from w13_gemv and exposes the w2 Marlin time alone. The real risks are implementation quality (Triton dequant ALU cost, early-exit grid, slot_list sizing) and geomean dilution, not interpretability.
justification: At bs=1 the parity result shows one Marlin line at 41.1 us (52.6% of 80.2 us), both GEMMs aggregated; w13 is ~27 us against a ~8 us w13-only floor (~30% of HBM), so a grouped GEMV reading each touched expert once has headroom; at bs=8 Marlin is 107.6 us, w13 share ~72 us against ~24 us. Expected shapes consistent with TASK.md (bs=1/8 faster, bs=16..256 untouched controls). cnt[e] <= M <= 8 fits BLOCK_M=16; cache1 row layout matches Marlin's so silu, w2 and post-norm are unaffected; e2m1 x e4m3 fits bf16 exactly. Weakest link: the Triton dequant speed (~15 ALU ops per weight with only ~256-512 live CTAs) could leave it slower than Marlin's lop3 tricks. At ~60% of HBM expect ~+6% geomean; at ~35-40% only 0.5-1%, inside the CI, so read per-shape medians. Second: +1 net launch and a mostly-empty grid cost a few us.
confounders: sglang-marlin-path-parity (the base): cannot be absent; its 32-expert align knob no longer feeds w13. Parity's unexplained 3 us bs=1 deficit vs SGLang may be partly recovered here; bounded <=0.7% of geomean, cannot flip a gain's sign; the SGLang column is a second yardstick.

~16 us of at::native glue at bs=1 of unknown origin: if part lives in the Marlin wrapper, dropping the w13 call removes it too and overstates the GEMV kernel's contribution; the profile shows this directly.
interference: No companion. ab-revert restores the 0.006x starter; ab-tune of the align knob resolves nothing; the per-kernel profile decomposes a loss (w13_gemv > ~27 us vs overhead) and a gain is unambiguous since bs=16..256 are untouched. Reading rule: judge on bs=1 and bs=8 medians against both parity (80.2 / 152.0 us) and SGLang (77.0 / 151.1 us); claim the mechanism only if the bs=1 gain exceeds ~5 us.
rules_flags: Apply the fp32 per-expert global scale after the K loop, not folded into the bf16 weight tile.
The prepare() weight copy is the same NVFP4 bytes, lossless; any K permutation must be applied consistently to scale gather and x column order. Prefer the natural layout with tl.interleave first.
cnt and slot_list must be rebuilt every call; allocate inside kernel_fn or ensure all 32 cnt entries are overwritten each call.
No host syncs; shape-fixed grid with device-side early exit. Do NOT use triton.autotune; fixed constexpr configs.
Only the lossless weight copy happens in prepare(), within budget.
bs=2..8 take the new path; cnt[e] <= M holds by construction.
open_questions: Record the standalone w2 Marlin time after this run so the w13 Marlin cost is measured, not inferred.
Where do the at::native reduce/elementwise launches at bs=1 come from?
Why is parity's bs=1 3.2 us slower than SGLang?
slot_list is sized cnt[e] <= 8 but the GEMV loads BLOCK_M=16 slots: pad to 16 columns or mask by arange < cnt before the x gather.
If the run loses with w13_gemv dominating, the follow-up should change only the dequant.
If w13_gemv is well above ~12 us at bs=1, smaller BLOCK_N or split-K is the next lever.
